evidence.quote: Most medium to large raptors consume whole vertebrate prey.

The best foods for birds of prey are mature mice and rats, because they contain a more complete nutrient profile than many other prey items; however, day-old chicks and other whole birds or mammal species also are adequate.
Owls should be fed day-old chicks, rats, or mice daily.
Although breeders regularly remove the egg yolk sac before feeding because it can cause hygienic problems when it breaks, the egg yolk of day-old chicks should not be removed when fed.
Commonly fed items include mice, rats, day-old chicks, quail, and pigeons, depending on the raptor species.
Feeding animals from the wild (eg, rats, pigeons, rabbits) is not advised, because these animals carry potential diseases, toxins, and poisons.
Prey with relatively large bones must be avoided because of the potential to cause obstruction in the gizzard, which prevents casting (regurgitation of the undigestible parts of prey).
Although breeders regularly remove the egg yolk sac before feeding because it can cause hygienic problems when it breaks, the egg yolk of day-old chicks should not be removed when fed.
Owls should be fed day-old chicks, rats, or mice daily.

Although whole prey, including organs, should be a complete, nutrient-sufficient feed, adding a small amount of a balanced vitamin and mineral supplement is advised, especially when birds are under stress.
Food items should not be thawed in warm water or they may grow undesirable bacteria; instead, food items should be thawed slowly in a refrigerator.

The term “angel wing” refers to carpal valgus deformity, a not uncommon condition where a bird’s wing (or wings) droops and then rotates outward.
While there are a number of factors that may contribute to the development of angel wing, nutritional factors, namely high levels of protein and carbohydrates, are a common cause.
If a resident starts showing signs of angel wing, be sure to consult with your veterinarian immediately, both to determine if the condition is correctable and also to determine the underlying cause.
Aspergillosis is a non-contagious fungal disease that typically manifests as respiratory illness in birds.
Signs of aspergillosis include open-mouth breathing, labored breathing, tail bobbing, gasping, and an elevated respiratory rate.
Poor ventilation, unsanitary conditions, wet bedding, moldy food, and warm, humid conditions increase the risk of aspergillosis.
Be sure to contact your veterinarian if you suspect aspergillosis.
Parvovirus of waterfowl is an infectious disease causing oculonasal exudates, watery diarrhea, and high mortality in young goslings and stunted growth and feather abnormalities in older goslings.

Not a difficult species to breed.
They should spawn the following morning. Only a few eggs are released at a time, so the event can often continue for several hours.
The water should be soft and acidic in the range pH 6.0-7.0, gH 1-10, with a temperature of around 24 – 26.5 °C 75 – 80 °F .
The adults will often eat their spawn given the chance and should be removed as soon as eggs are noticed. These will hatch in 24-36 hours, with the fry becoming free swimming 4-5 days later.
This should be very dimly lit and contain clumps of fine-leaved plants such as java moss or spawning mops, to give the fish somewhere to deposit their eggs.
